text: Attempt 2 starts on the same map as attempt 1, using its lessons: water from day one, a road grid instead of one main road, an early link to a neighbor city, low taxes, and a health check (water, power, abandoned buildings, traffic jams) every game year.
Coal power plant (200 MW) in the southeast by the river, so power won't run out as the city grows.
Road grid: 4 east-west roads and 5 north-south roads, so traffic has many routes. Power and water lines run north-south through the middle of each block.
10 water pumps on day one: 5 on the lake shore, 5 on the river next to the plant.
Zoned dense residential on the west half (144 tiles), light industry next to the plant (~96 tiles), and only a small shop block (24 tiles).
Tax set to 5% from the start (attempt 1 sat at 7% for 25 years).
Road to the west map edge: trade connection with Fort Verdegris ($1,000).
Year 1 health check: only 30% of buildings had water. The eastern pipe columns weren't linked to the pumps. Added the missing links within the first year (attempt 1 took 8 years to spot this).
Shop demand turned positive (+1,650) in 2002, so zoned one more 24-tile shop block in the middle of town.

2003: factories were over-built (industry demand -1,825, 35 abandoned) while housing demand was maxed. Built a north district by the lake instead: 2 roads, 3 links, ~150 dense residential tiles, power, pipes and 2 lake pumps.
2005: housing demand -2,000 and unemployment 17%: the city needs jobs. Added a 50-tile factory strip on a new road east of the lake, plus one more row of shops.
Jan 2007, pop 3,280 (attempt 1 had 1,450 at this point): zoned another ~60 dense residential tiles north of the north district, with power and pipes.
Health check 2008: the east factory strip's far side had no power (a road separated it from the line). Added 3 power crossings, and zoned 14 more factory tiles by the plant.

2010: ~30 dense homes abandoned in the north district despite power, water, no crime and no pollution. Likely cause: long commutes, since the district's only road link ran around the lake. Added a direct road on the east side of the lake to the factories.
Jan 2012, pop 4,820: shop and factory demand both maxed. Zoned a 60-tile shop district west of the west road, next to the north homes, with power crossings and pipes.

2013 setback: pop fell to 4,570 and unemployment hit 25%. Homes had outgrown jobs and every factory zone was full. Rezoned the mostly-abandoned southwest housing band as industry and zoned a 37-tile factory strip along the south edge.
GOAL 1 REACHED: 5,970 people in Jan 2015, 15 years into the 30-year limit (attempt 1 never got there). No bonds ever taken.
